items.title: Diagonal spectrum
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be a complete orthonormal family of $H$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]), let $(\lambda_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\subseteq\mathbb R$, and let $A$ be the self-adjoint diagonal operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]]:

$$D(A)=\Bigl\{x\in H:\sum_{n}\lambda_n^2|\langle x,e_n\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad Ax=\sum_{n}\lambda_n\langle x,e_n\rangle e_n .$$

Then, with $\rho(A)$, $\sigma(A)$ and $R(\lambda,A)$ as in [[def-resolvent-of-a-closed-operator]]:

(a) $Ae_n=\lambda_ne_n$ for every $n$; every $\lambda_n$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, hence belongs to $\sigma(A)$;

(b) $\sigma(A)=\overline{\{\lambda_n:n\in\mathbb N\}}$, the closure in $\mathbb C$; equivalently $\lambda\in\rho(A)$ exactly when $d:=\inf_n|\lambda-\lambda_n|>0$, and then

$$R(\lambda,A)x=\sum_{n}(\lambda-\lambda_n)^{-1}\langle x,e_n\rangle e_n,\qquad \|R(\lambda,A)\|=d^{-1}=\bigl(\inf_n|\lambda-\lambda_n|\bigr)^{-1};$$

(c) if $\lambda\in\sigma(A)\setminus\{\lambda_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$, then $\lambda$ is an approximate eigenvalue: for some subsequence $(n_k)$, $\|(\lambda I-A)e_{n_k}\|\to0$ with $\|e_{n_k}\|=1$. Moreover, $\ker(\lambda I-A)=\{0\}$, so $\lambda$ is not an eigenvalue of $A$; no further identification of spectral types is made.

items.title: Hermite recurrence
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $L^2=L^2(\mathbb R,dy)$ be the complex Lebesgue space with inner product $\langle\varphi,\psi\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R}\varphi(y)\overline{\psi(y)}\,dy$ linear in the first argument ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]], [[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]); this pairing makes $L^2$ a complex Hilbert space by [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]. For complex-valued functions, smoothness and derivatives use the componentwise convention of [[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]. Write $g_0$ for the function $g_0(y):=\pi^{-1/4}e^{-y^{2}/2}$ and also for its class in $L^2$. Put

$$P:=\{p\,g_0:\ p\in\mathbb C[y]\}\subseteq L^2 ,$$

the set of classes of polynomial multiples of $g_0$. Each class in $P$ has a unique representative of the form $p g_0$: if $p g_0=qg_0$ almost everywhere, the continuous function $(p-q)g_0$ vanishes almost everywhere and therefore everywhere, and $g_0(y)>0$ for every $y$, so $p=q$. Let $Y$ be multiplication by $y$ and $\partial_y$ the derivative, acting on this unique smooth representative. Set $g_{-1}:=0$ for use in the recurrence formulas at $n=0$. Define

$$a:=\frac{Y+\partial_y}{\sqrt2},\qquad a^\dagger:=\frac{Y-\partial_y}{\sqrt2},\qquad g_n:=\frac{(a^\dagger)^ng_0}{\sqrt{n!}}\quad(n\in\mathbb N).$$

Then:

(a) $g_0\in L^2$ with $\|g_0\|=1$; more generally $y^kg_0\in L^2$ for every $k\in\mathbb N$, so $P$ is a linear subspace of $L^2$ all of whose members are represented by $C^\infty$ functions;

(b) $Y,\partial_y,a,a^\dagger$ map $P$ into $P$, and $\partial_y(pg_0)=(p'-yp)g_0$ for every polynomial $p$;

(c) for all $\varphi,\psi\in P$, $\langle a^\dagger\varphi,\psi\rangle=\langle\varphi,a\psi\rangle$ and $\langle a\varphi,\psi\rangle=\langle\varphi,a^\dagger\psi\rangle$;

(d) $a^\dagger a-a a^\dagger=-I$ on $P$, i.e. $[a,a^\dagger]=aa^\dagger-a^\dagger a=I$ on $P$, and $ag_0=0$;

(e) for every $n\in\mathbb N$: $ag_n=\sqrt n\,g_{n-1}$ (with $ag_0=0$), $a^\dagger g_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,g_{n+1}$, $a^\dagger ag_n=ng_n$ and $aa^\dagger g_n=(n+1)g_n$;

(f) the polynomials

$$H_n(y):=(-1)^ne^{y^2}\frac{d^n}{dy^n}e^{-y^2}$$

are polynomials of degree $n$ with leading coefficient $2^n$, $H_0=1$, $H_1(y)=2y$, $H_n(-y)=(-1)^nH_n(y)$, and they satisfy

$$H_n'=2nH_{n-1},\qquad H_{n+1}=2yH_n-2nH_{n-1}\qquad(n\ge1);$$

moreover

$$g_n=\frac{H_ng_0}{\sqrt{2^nn!}};$$

(g) consequently

$$\sqrt2\,y\,g_n=\sqrt n\,g_{n-1}+\sqrt{n+1}\,g_{n+1},\qquad \sqrt2\,g_n'=\sqrt n\,g_{n-1}-\sqrt{n+1}\,g_{n+1}.$$

items.title: Hermite orthogonality
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $L^2=L^2(\mathbb R,dy)$ be the complex Lebesgue space with inner product linear in the first argument, and let $g_0,P,a,a^\dagger,g_n$ and $H_n$ be as in [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-recurrence]]. Then, for all $m,n\in\mathbb N$:

(a) $\langle g_n,g_m\rangle=\delta_{nm}$; in particular $(g_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is an orthonormal family in $L^2$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]);

(b) the eigenvalue equation $(-\partial_y^2+Y^2)g_n=(2n+1)g_n$ holds as an identity of $L^2$ classes; more precisely $Y^2-\partial_y^2=2a^\dagger a+I$ as operators on $P$, so that on $P$

$$-\varphi''+y^2\varphi=2a^\dagger a\varphi+\varphi\qquad(\varphi\in P);$$

(c) $\langle ag_n,ag_m\rangle=n\,\delta_{nm}$ and $\langle a^\dagger g_n,a^\dagger g_m\rangle=(n+1)\delta_{nm}$ for all $n,m\in\mathbb N$.

No completeness of the family $(g_n)$ is asserted here.

items.title: Oscillator scaling and exact realization
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix real parameters $m>0$, $\omega>0$, $\hbar>0$, put $\ell:=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}>0$, and let $g_0,P,(g_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be the Hermite data of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-recurrence]] in $L^2(\mathbb R,dy)$, so that $(g_n)$ is a complete orthonormal family by [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-completeness]]. Define

$$D:L^2(\mathbb R,dy)\to L^2(\mathbb R,dx),\qquad (Df)(x):=\ell^{-1/2}f(x/\ell),$$

and let $A$ be the self-adjoint diagonal operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]] for the complete orthonormal family $(g_n)$ and the eigenvalues $\lambda_n=2n+1$, with the core $P$ and spectrum $\{2n+1:n\in\mathbb N\}$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-spectrum]]).

Then:

(a) $D$ is a linear isometry of $L^2(\mathbb R,dy)$ onto $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$ with two-sided inverse $(D^{-1}g)(y)=\ell^{1/2}g(\ell y)$; the functions $\psi_n:=Dg_n$, $\psi_n(x)=\ell^{-1/2}g_n(x/\ell)$, form a complete orthonormal family of $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$;

(b) the operator

$$H_{\mathrm{osc}}:=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\,DAD^{-1},\qquad D(H_{\mathrm{osc}}):=\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R,dx):D^{-1}f\in D(A)\},$$

is self-adjoint, satisfies $H_{\mathrm{osc}}\psi_n=\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)\psi_n$ for every $n$, and has

$$D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})=\Bigl\{f:\sum_n\hbar^2\omega^2(n+\tfrac12)^2|c_n|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad H_{\mathrm{osc}}f=\sum_n\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)c_n\psi_n,$$

where $c_n:=\langle D^{-1}f,g_n\rangle=\langle f,\psi_n\rangle$; its spectrum is $\sigma(H_{\mathrm{osc}})=\{\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12):n\in\mathbb N\}$, its ground energy is $\hbar\omega/2$ with eigenvector $\psi_0$, and $\langle H_{\mathrm{osc}}f,f\rangle\ge\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\|f\|^2$ for every $f\in D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$;

(c) $D(P)=\operatorname{span}\{\psi_n\}$ is a core for $H_{\mathrm{osc}}$, and for every polynomial $p$ the function $f:=D(pg_0)$ is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R$ with

$$H_{\mathrm{osc}}f=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}f''+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}x^2f$$

pointwise on $\mathbb R$;

(d) for every $f\in D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ and every test function $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$,

$$\int_{\mathbb R}(H_{\mathrm{osc}}f)(x)\varphi(x)\,dx=\int_{\mathbb R}f(x)\Bigl(-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\varphi''(x)+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}x^2\varphi(x)\Bigr)dx,$$

so $H_{\mathrm{osc}}$ is the self-adjoint realization of the differential expression $-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\frac{d^2}{dx^2}+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}x^2$ in the weak sense; no identification of $D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ with a separately defined maximal differential-operator domain is asserted.

All parameters enter as positive real numbers; no physical identification of $m,\omega,\hbar$ with measured quantities is made.

items.title: Coherent evolution and variance
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $m,\omega,\hbar>0$ and let $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, $D$, $\psi_n=Dg_n$, $H_{\mathrm{osc}}=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}DAD^{-1}$ be as in [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]], with $(g_n)$ the Hermite family and $a,a^\dagger,N$ the closed ladder and number operators of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]]; put $a_\psi:=DaD^{-1}$, $a^\dagger_\psi:=Da^\dagger D^{-1}$, $N_\psi:=DND^{-1}$, acting on $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$ with the transported domains, and for $z\in\mathbb C$ let $\psi_z^{(y)}\in L^2(\mathbb R,dy)$ be the coherent vector of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-convergence]] and define $\psi_z:=D\psi_z^{(y)}=e^{-|z|^2/2}\sum_nz^n\psi_n/\sqrt{n!}\in L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$. Finally set

$$Q:=M_x,\quad D(Q)=\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R,dx):xf\in L^2\},\qquad P:=\mathcal F_2^*M_{2\pi\hbar\xi}\mathcal F_2,\quad D(P)=\{f:\xi\,\mathcal F_2f\in L^2\},$$

the self-adjoint position and momentum operators ([[lem-real-ltwo-multipliers-and-unitary-transport]], [[thm-plancherel]]; the conjugation is discharged in the proof).

Then:

(a) $H_{\mathrm{osc}}=\hbar\omega(N_\psi+\tfrac12I)$ as operators, with common domain $D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})=D(N_\psi)$;

(b) the formula

$$U(t)f:=\sum_{n}e^{-i\omega(n+1/2)t}\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\psi_n\qquad(t\in\mathbb R,\ f\in L^2(\mathbb R,dx))$$

defines a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group $U$ on $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$: each $U(t)$ is a surjective linear isometry, $U(0)=I$ and $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$, and the generator of $U$ is $-\tfrac{i}{\hbar}H_{\mathrm{osc}}$, i.e. the limit $\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t(U(t)f-f)$ exists exactly for $f\in D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ and equals $-\tfrac{i}{\hbar}H_{\mathrm{osc}}f$;

(c) $U(t)\psi_z=e^{-i\omega t/2}\psi_{ze^{-i\omega t}}$ for all $z\in\mathbb C$, $t\in\mathbb R$;

(d) on the orthonormal basis one has

$$Q\psi_n=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}\bigl(\sqrt{n+1}\,\psi_{n+1}+\sqrt n\,\psi_{n-1}\bigr),\qquad P\psi_n=\frac{\hbar}{i\ell\sqrt2}\bigl(\sqrt n\,\psi_{n-1}-\sqrt{n+1}\,\psi_{n+1}\bigr),$$

with the convention $\psi_{-1}:=0$; consequently, for every $z\in\mathbb C$,

$$Q\psi_z=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}\,(a_\psi+a^\dagger_\psi)\psi_z,\qquad P\psi_z=\frac{\hbar}{i\ell\sqrt2}\,(a_\psi-a^\dagger_\psi)\psi_z ;$$

(e) with means $\langle Q\rangle_z:=\langle Q\psi_z,\psi_z\rangle$, $\langle P\rangle_z:=\langle P\psi_z,\psi_z\rangle$ and variances $\operatorname{Var}(Q)_z:=\|(Q-\langle Q\rangle_zI)\psi_z\|^2$, $\operatorname{Var}(P)_z:=\|(P-\langle P\rangle_zI)\psi_z\|^2$,

$$\langle Q\rangle_z=\sqrt2\,\ell\operatorname{Re}z,\quad\langle P\rangle_z=\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z,\quad\operatorname{Var}(Q)_z=\frac{\ell^2}{2},\quad\operatorname{Var}(P)_z=\frac{\hbar^2}{2\ell^2},$$

so $\operatorname{Var}(Q)_z\operatorname{Var}(P)_z=\hbar^2/4$ for every $z$ (the value produced by these exact computations; no independent uncertainty-bound statement is asserted here);

(f) after the evolution, with $\psi_z(t):=U(t)\psi_z$ and $z(t):=ze^{-i\omega t}$,

$$\langle Q\rangle_{z(t)}=\sqrt2\,\ell\operatorname{Re}z(t),\quad\langle P\rangle_{z(t)}=\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z(t),\quad\operatorname{Var}(Q)_{z(t)}=\frac{\ell^2}{2},\quad\operatorname{Var}(P)_{z(t)}=\frac{\hbar^2}{2\ell^2}.$$

The parameters $m,\omega,\hbar$ enter as positive real numbers and no physical identification of $Q,P,H_{\mathrm{osc}}$ with measured quantities is made.

items.title: Multidimensional oscillator completeness
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $d\ge1$. For each $j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$ put $K_j^y:=L^2(\mathbb R,dy_j)$ and take a copy $(g^{(j)}_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ of the Hermite family of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-recurrence]] in $K_j^y$. Define the left-associated completed tensor products by $\mathcal K_1^y:=K_1^y$ and $\mathcal K_r^y:=\mathcal K_{r-1}^y\widehat\otimes K_r^y$ for $2\le r\le d$. Let $\Theta_y^{(1)}:K_1^y\to L^2(\mathbb R,dy_1)$ be the identity; recursively, for $2\le r\le d$, let

$$\Theta_y^{(r)}:=\Theta_{r-1,1}^y\circ\bigl(\Theta_y^{(r-1)}\otimes I_{K_r^y}\bigr):\mathcal K_r^y\longrightarrow L^2(\mathbb R^r,dy),$$

where $\Theta_{r-1,1}^y:L^2(\mathbb R^{r-1},dy)\widehat\otimes K_r^y\to L^2(\mathbb R^r,dy)$ is the two-factor Euclidean product unitary of [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]], and $\Theta_y^{(r-1)}\otimes I_{K_r^y}$ is the bounded tensor map of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]]. Thus $\Theta_y^{(r)}$ is a specified unitary, with $\Theta_y^{(r)}(u\otimes v)(y',y_r)=\Theta_y^{(r-1)}u(y')v(y_r)$ almost everywhere. For $N=(n_1,\dots,n_d)\in\mathbb N^d$, set $G_N^{y,1}:=g^{(1)}_{n_1}$ and recursively $G_N^{y,r}:=G_N^{y,r-1}\otimes g^{(r)}_{n_r}$; define $g_N:=\Theta_y^{(d)}G_N^{y,d}\in L^2(\mathbb R^d,dy)$.

Let $\varphi:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N^d$ list the multi-indices by increasing total degree $M=\sum_jn_j$ and, within each finite level, in lexicographic order. By [[thm-stars-and-bars]] each level is finite and the levels exhaust $\mathbb N^d$, so this specifies a bijection. All sums indexed by $\mathbb N^d$ below are taken in this order; nonnegative sums equivalently mean the supremum of finite subsums.

The functions $g_N$ have smooth product representatives from the recursive construction. These representatives are unique: a continuous difference that is nonzero at a point remains nonzero on a ball of positive Lebesgue measure. The coordinate derivatives in (b) and (c) are taken on these representatives and their scaled products.

Then:

(a) $(g_N)_{N\in\mathbb N^d}$ is a complete orthonormal family of $L^2(\mathbb R^d,dy)$: $\langle g_N,g_M\rangle=\delta_{NM}$ and every $f\in L^2(\mathbb R^d,dy)$ has $f=\sum_{N\in\mathbb N^d}\langle f,g_N\rangle g_N$ with $\|f\|^2=\sum_{N\in\mathbb N^d}|\langle f,g_N\rangle|^2$, the sum being the supremum over finite subfamilies ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]], [[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]]);

(b) with the eigenvalues $\lambda_N:=\sum_{j=1}^d(2n_j+1)=2M+d$, $M:=\sum_jn_j$, let $A_d$ be the diagonal operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]] for the enumerated family $e_m:=g_{\varphi(m)}$ and eigenvalue sequence $\lambda_{\varphi(m)}$. Then $A_d$ is self-adjoint with

$$A_dg_N=\lambda_Ng_N,\qquad D(A_d)=\Bigl\{f:\sum_{N\in\mathbb N^d}\lambda_N^2|\langle f,g_N\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad \sigma(A_d)=\{2M+d:M\in\mathbb N\}$$

(the spectrum by [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-spectrum]]); the algebraic span of the $g_N$ is a core, and on that span

$$A_d=\sum_{j=1}^d\bigl(-\partial_{y_j}^2+y_j^2\bigr)$$

as operators, the $j$-th summand acting in the $j$-th coordinate;

(c) for real $m_j,\omega_j,\hbar>0$ put $\ell_j:=\sqrt{\hbar/(m_j\omega_j)}$ and let $D_j:K_j^y\to K_j^x:=L^2(\mathbb R,dx_j)$ be the one-dimensional unitary of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]]. Define $\mathcal K_1^x:=K_1^x$ and $\mathcal K_r^x:=\mathcal K_{r-1}^x\widehat\otimes K_r^x$ for $2\le r\le d$, and define $\Theta_x^{(1)}$ and $\Theta_x^{(r)}$ by the same recursion as $\Theta_y^{(r)}$, using the two-factor Euclidean product unitaries on the $x$-coordinate spaces. Let $\mathcal D_1:=D_1$ and recursively $\mathcal D_r:=\mathcal D_{r-1}\otimes D_r:\mathcal K_r^y\to\mathcal K_r^x$; each $\mathcal D_r$ is unitary by [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]]. Put $D_d:=\Theta_x^{(d)}\mathcal D_d(\Theta_y^{(d)})^{-1}:L^2(\mathbb R^d,dy)\to L^2(\mathbb R^d,dx)$. For $N\in\mathbb N^d$, define $G_N^{x,1}:=D_1g^{(1)}_{n_1}=:\psi^{(1)}_{n_1}$ and recursively $G_N^{x,r}:=G_N^{x,r-1}\otimes\psi^{(r)}_{n_r}$; then $\psi_N:=D_dg_N=\Theta_x^{(d)}G_N^{x,d}$. Let $H$ be the diagonal operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]] for the enumerated family $\psi_{\varphi(m)}$ and eigenvalue sequence $E_{\varphi(m)}$, where $E_N:=\hbar\sum_{j=1}^d\omega_j(n_j+\frac12)$. Then $H$ is self-adjoint with

$$H\psi_N=E_N\psi_N,\qquad D(H)=\Bigl\{f:\sum_N E_N^2|\langle f,\psi_N\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad \sigma(H)=\overline{\{E_N:N\in\mathbb N^d\}},$$

the span of the $\psi_N$ is a core, and on that core

$$H=\sum_{j=1}^d\Bigl(-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m_j}\partial_{x_j}^2+\frac{m_j\omega_j^2}{2}x_j^2\Bigr);$$

(d) if $\omega_1=\cdots=\omega_d=\omega$, then $\sigma(H)=\{\hbar\omega(M+\frac d2):M\in\mathbb N\}$, and the eigenvalue $\hbar\omega(M+\frac d2)$ has multiplicity

$$\bigl|\{(n_1,\dots,n_d)\in\mathbb N^d:n_1+\cdots+n_d=M\}\bigr|=\binom{M+d-1}{d-1};$$

in particular for $d=3$ the multiplicity is $(M+1)(M+2)/2$ ([[thm-stars-and-bars]]). All parameters are positive real numbers; no physical interpretation is asserted.

items.title: Ground energy units
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $m,\omega,\hbar>0$ and let $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, $\psi_n$, $H_{\mathrm{osc}}$ be as in [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]]. Then:

(a) the spectrum of $H_{\mathrm{osc}}$ is exactly $\{\hbar\omega(n+\frac12):n\in\mathbb N\}$; measured in units of $\hbar\omega$ the eigenvalues are $n+\frac12$, the ground energy is

$$\frac{E_0}{\hbar\omega}=\frac12,$$

and every consecutive gap is $1$ unit: $\frac{E_{n+1}-E_n}{\hbar\omega}=1$;

(b) the ground eigenvector is the Gaussian

$$\psi_0(x)=\pi^{-1/4}\ell^{-1/2}e^{-x^2/(2\ell^2)},$$

and it satisfies the eigenvalue equation pointwise:

$$-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\psi_0''(x)+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}x^2\psi_0(x)=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\psi_0(x)\qquad(x\in\mathbb R);$$

(c) for the isotropic $d$-dimensional oscillator of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-multidimensional-oscillator-completeness]]$\,$(d) with common frequency $\omega$, the ground energy is $\frac{d}{2}\hbar\omega$ in the same units, in particular $\frac32\hbar\omega$ for $d=3$, and all gaps within one coordinate direction are $\hbar\omega$;

(d) no other value of the ground energy is compatible with the displayed spectrum: $E_0$ is the infimum of $\sigma(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$.

No physical identification of $\hbar\omega$ with a measured energy is made; the statements are about the operator $H_{\mathrm{osc}}$ built from the positive parameters.

items.title: Formal nonnormalizable solution
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $g_0(y)=\pi^{-1/4}e^{-y^2/2}$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-recurrence]](a)) and define

$$F(y):=\int_0^ye^{t^2}\,dt,\qquad u_2(y):=e^{-y^2/2}F(y)\qquad(y\in\mathbb R).$$

Then:

(a) $F$ is $C^1$ with $F'=e^{y^2}$, and $u_2$ is $C^2$ and solves the ground-state eigenvalue equation

$$u_2''(y)=(y^2-1)u_2(y)\qquad(y\in\mathbb R),$$

which is the equation $(-\partial_y^2+y^2)u=u$ satisfied by $g_0$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-orthogonality]](b));

(b) the Wronskian is constant and nonzero,

$$W:=g_0u_2'-g_0'u_2=\pi^{-1/4},$$

so $g_0$ and $u_2$ are linearly independent solutions;

(c) $u_2\notin L^2(\mathbb R,dy)$: for $y\ge1$ one has $|u_2(y)|^2\ge e^{y^2-4y+2}$, which is not integrable, so $\int_{\mathbb R}|u_2|^2dy=+\infty$;

(d) every $C^2$ function $u:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ (with complex smoothness and derivatives understood componentwise as in [[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]) that belongs to $L^2(\mathbb R,dy)$ and solves $u''=(y^2-1)u$ is a constant multiple of $g_0$: the quantity $W(u):=g_0u'-g_0'u$ is constant for such $u$; if this constant is nonzero then $u(y)=g_0(y)\bigl(C+c\pi^{1/2}F(y)\bigr)$ for some constants with $c\ne0$, which satisfies $|u(y)|\ge K e^{y^2/2-2y+1}$ for some $K>0$ and all sufficiently large $y$, and is not in $L^2$; hence the constant is zero and $u/g_0$ is constant.

Thus $u_2$ is the classical formal second solution of the ground-state equation, and its failure to be square-integrable is what forces the $L^2$ eigenfunction to be the Gaussian.
